text.p: These are the leading stories in the Albanian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

All newspapers carry coverage of the attempt against President Sali Berisha. A hand grenade was thrown at Berisha as he adressed a rally in a village near Durres, but it was deactivated. No casualties were reported.
- The paper says 30 children have been killed and 600 injured over the past few months.
- Socialist and Social Democratic parties joined forces in an electoral alliance to oust President Sali Berisha's Democratic Party at the June elections.
- Albert Shyti, leader of so-called committee of public salvation in Vlore, warned President Sali Berisha not to dare visit the town which he claimed was terrorised by Berisha's criminal gangs.
- Some 1,600 Italian soldiers and 1,000 Belgians will join the 6,500-strong multinational force in Albania to secure the voting process.
- Gangland violence has taken the death toll to dozens this week, with hundreds injured across the country.
- Union for Democracy, an anti-communist electoral alliance of the Democratic Party and the rightest and centrist parties, will hold a rally in Tirana on Friday.
- Great Britain will send 45 observers to monitor early elections set for June 29.
- TNT explosions rocked the northeastern town of Kukes.
- The national road linking the southern town of Berat and the capital Tirana has been blocked following fire exchange between armed gangs.
- The OSCE mission to monitor the upcoming elections opened an office in the southernmost town of Gjirokaster.
- President Sali Berisha criticised Prime Minister Bashkim Fino during an electoral campaign, saying his national reconciliation government failed in re-establishing order and peace in the country.
- Democratic Alliance Party leader Neritan Ceka accused a delegation from the European Parliament of favouring President Berisha and his Democratic Party.
- An editorial slams Albanian authorities for failing to protest against anti-Albanian acts of the Former Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia.
